messages:
Anya G: heads up — ran a sim of regional preemption + model-variant downgrade, results look worrying for mid-tier customers. latency SLOs spike when preemption happens in eu-west-1 and we fall back to smaller quantized variants.
Rob C: can you paste the sim config/results? curious if batching or cache TTLs changed the shape.
Anya G: gist of config below. used the policy that preempts to best-effort when region capacity < 12% of committed. fallback to m1-quant then m1-8bit. observed 90p latency jump ~300ms.
```yaml
policy: 
  preemption_threshold: 0.12  # fraction of reserved capacity
  tier_routes:
    - tier: premium
      region_order: [primary, failover]
      allow_preempt: false
    - tier: mid
      region_order: [primary, best-effort]
      allow_preempt: true
  fallback_map:
    m1: [m1-quant, m1-8bit]
    m2: [m2-8bit]
```
Rob C: hmm — mid-tier allow_preempt true makes sense for cost, but we need headroom knobs so mid-tier doesn't see SLA blowouts. maybe per-tenant preemption_budget + min_latency_guard?
Sam L: +1. we already have per-tenant quotas but not a soft-latency-budget. proposal: preemption_budget is expressed in rps or tokens per minute that can be preempted before we trigger protective routing.
Lucy M: how would that interact with circuit-breaker windows? currently CB trips on 5xx rate or latency > 95p for 30s. if we add preemption, CB would need awareness of fallback-induced latency vs actual infra failures.
Anya G: that's the UX problem — operators and SEs see a CB trip and assume infra outage. we should differentiate "policy-induced degradation" from "service degradation" in telemetry and console alerts.
Infra Bot: deploy-check: routing-policy v0.9.1 staged to canary (3 nodes eu-west-1) at 2026-03-15T14:32Z.
Rob C: idea: add a boolean flag in CB state -> reason: [latency_infra, policy_fallback, model_unavailable]. show in console traces and in incident summary.
Sam L: for the console simulation page, we should let users run a "what-if preemption" with sliders: capacity %, fallback depth, per-tenant budget. simulate token-cost and latency percentile impact.
Lucy M: agree. also show expected cost delta (tokens and $$) and a suggested mitigation: increase reserved capacity or bump mid-tier fallback threshold to use regional failover first.
Mohit P: on API surface — we need a small extension for routing hints: 
- preemption_budget (int tokens/min)
- latency_guard_ms (int)
- allow_fallback_variants (list)
This should be optional and default to current behavior.
Anya G: pinging @Sam L and @Mohit P for API + console mock. Can we prototype a small UI flow in the console that ties policy -> sim -> one-click apply (staging only)?
Sam L: yes I can mock. rough plan: new pane in model routing tab: "SLO-driven preemption" with: slider for preemption budget, toggle for show-sim, button "run sim" -> output heatmap of p50/p95/p99 across regions.
Rob C: telemetry: we need a new metric series: policy_fallback_rate{tier,region,variant} and a derived metric: policy_fallback_latency_impact{tier}. also mark traces with routing_reason tag to help SLO ownership.
Lucy M: for rollouts, can we gate policy changes behind canary plus traffic-shift that's aware of customer tier? i.e., apply to 10% of mid-tier customers first.
Anya G: exactly. smaller question: what's the circuit-breaker threshold when fallback is in play? we should be more lenient for policy_fallback_reason for a short window so CB doesn't overreact. maybe double latency threshold for first 60s after fallback starts.
Rob C: acceptable if we add visibility and an auto-revert if latency stays bad for >5m. also emit an event to the rollout system so it marks that change as risky.
Mohit P: I'll draft API PR that adds the three fields and emits telemetry tags. will include migration notes.
Sam L: I'll sketch console mock by EOD. can we target a small end-to-end demo for next sprint: policy UI -> run sim -> apply to staging -> watch telemetry with new tags?
Anya G: yes. I'll create a short playbook for SEs describing what to do if mid-tier customers see >200ms regression after policy change. include how to quickly pin model variants and reduce preemption_budget.
Rob C: one last nit — ensure the sim accounts for KV cache hit rate. fallback to smaller variants often bypasses large KV caches and causes token re-compute. simulate both cache preserved and cache-miss scenarios.
Anya G: noted. thanks all. tagging this thread for the console/telemetry sync. :white_check_mark:
